newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvian finmin gets parliament backing.
newsitem.headline: New Latvian finmin gets parliament backing.

text.p: New Latvian Finance Minister Robert Zile was voted into office by parliament on Thursday, filling a post that has been vacant since October.
Parliament backed Zile's appointment with 68 votes in favour, four against and no absentions out of the 100-seat chamber, the parliament press office said.
Zile is from For Fatherland and Freedom, the third largest of the eight parties in the coalition government, and is currently head of the parliamentary budget and finance committee.
His main task will be to achieve a plan to balance budget this year.

Arguments over the finance post caused the collapse of the previous government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele when President Guntis Ulmanis called on parliament to reject one of Shkele's previous candidates for the post.
Shkele resigned but he and the president settled their differences and Shkele formed a new government.
